about: Buzz Lightyear wraps an arm around a nervous, wide-eyed Woody and sweeps his other hand toward the horizon, smiling as if showing off a glorious view. The meme uses the snowclone "X, X everywhere": the top line names something and the bottom line declares it is everywhere. Buzz's enthusiasm against Woody's visible discomfort sets the tone, so it is used to point out something that has become impossible to avoid, whether that is exciting or deeply annoying.
origin: The still comes from Pixar's Toy Story (1995). The "X, X everywhere" caption format was a widely shared image macro by the early 2010s.
usage:
Put the subject in the top box, a single word or short noun phrase like "pumpkin spice". The bottom box repeats it with "everywhere": "pumpkin spice everywhere". The repetition is the format, so keep the exact same wording in both lines.

It works for trends, seasonal flooding of the same thing, and problems that multiply: ads, spoilers, bugs, influencers, construction cones, new streaming services. Picture Woody as the person who has to deal with it and Buzz as the one who loves it.
